ρα.def: ῥα (epic for ἄρα) enclit. Particle, Hom., and in lyric passages of Trag.

ραββι.def: ῥαββί o my master, Hebr. words in NTest.

ραβδιον.def: ῥαβδίον, ου, τό, (Dim. of ῥάβδος) a little rod, a wand, Babr.

ραβδομαχια.def: ῥαβδο-μᾰχία, ἡ, (μάχομαι) a fighting with a staff or foil, Plut.

ραβδονομεω.def: ῥαβδονομέω, to sit as umpire, Soph. (from ῥαβδονόμος)

ραβδονομοσ.def: ῥαβδο-νόμος, ον, (νέμω) holding a rod or wand; hence, like ῥαβδοῦχος, of the Rom. lictors, Plut.

ραβδοσ.def: ῥάβδος, ἡ, I. a rod, wand, stick, switch, Lat. virga, Hom., Xen. 2. a magic wand, as that of Circe or Hermes, Hom. 3. a fishing-rod, Od.:—also a limed twig, for catching birds, Ar. 4. a spear-staff or shaft, Xen. 5. a staff of office, like the earlier σκῆπτρον, Pind. 6. the wand borne by the ῥαψῳδός: hence, κατὰ ῥάβδον ἐπέων according to the measure of his (Homer's) verses, Pind. 7. a rod for chastisement, Plat.; αἱ ῥάβδοι the fasces of the Roman lictors, Plut. II. a stripe or strip, Il.

ραβδουχεω.def: ῥαβδουχέω, (from ῥαβδοῦχος) to carry a rod or wand, as a badge of office:—Pass., at Rome, to have the fasces borne before one, Plut.

ραβδουχια.def: ῥαβδουχία, ἡ, at Rome, the fasces, Plut. (from ῥαβδοῦχος)

ραβδουχοσ.def: ῥαβδ-οῦχος, ὁ, (ἔχω) one who carries a rod or staff of office: 1. a judge, umpire at a contest, Plat. 2. a magistrate's attendant, a beadle, Ar.:—so, at Rome, of the lictors who carried the fasces, Polyb., etc.

ραβδοφορεω.def: ῥαβδοφορέω, to carry a wand or stick, Strab. (from ῥαβδοφόρος)

ραβδωσισ.def: ῥάβδωσις, εως, (as if from ῥαβδόω) the fluting of columns, Arist. (cf. ῥαβδωτός)

ραβδωτοσ.def: ῥαβδωτός, ή, όν (as if from ῥαβδόω) (cf. ῥάβδος II) striped, Xen.

ραγασ.def: ῥᾰγάς, άδος, (ῥαγῆναι) a rent, chink, Anth.

ραγδαιοσ.def: ῥαγδαῖος, η, ον (ῥάγδην) tearing, furious, Plut., Luc.

ραγολογοσ.def: ῥᾱγο-λόγος, ον, (ῥάξ, λέγω) gathering berries, Anth.

ραδινακη.def: ῥαδινάκη, ἡ, the Persian name for a black strong smelling petroleum, Hdt.

ραδινοσ.def: ῥᾰδῐνός, ή, όν 1. slender, taper, Il., Theogn., etc. 2. of the limbs or body, taper, slim, Hes., Theogn. 3. generally, tender or mobile, ὄσσε Aesch.

ραδιοσ.def: ῥᾴδιος, η, ον I. easy, ready, easy to make or do, opp. to χαλεπός, Hom., etc.; ῥηίδιόν τοι ἔπος a word easy for thee to understand, Od.:—c. inf., τάφρος ῥηιδίη περῆσαι easy to pass over, Il.; ῥηίτεροι πολεμίζειν easier to fight with, id. 2. ῥᾴδιόν ἐστι it is easy to do a thing, c. inf., Pind., Thuc.; c. acc. et inf., τύραννον εὐσεβεῖν οὐ ῥᾴδιον Soph.; also, ῥᾷστοί εἰσιν ἀμύνεσθαι ῥᾴδιόν ἐστιν αὐτοὺς ἀμύνεσθαι, Thuc. b. also, ῥᾴδιόν ἐστι it is a light matter, you think little of doing, παρ’ ὑμῖν ῥ. ξενοκτονεῖν Eur. II. of persons, easy, complaisant, Lat. facilis, commodus, Dem.:—in bad sense, reckless, Luc. B. adv. ῥᾳδίως, epic and ionic ῥηιδίως, easily, lightly, readily, willingly, Hom., etc.; ῥᾳδίως φέρειν to bear lightly, make light of a thing, Eur., etc. 2. in bad sense, lightly, recklessly, rashly, Thuc.; ῥᾳδίως οὕτω in this easy, thoughtless way, Plat. II. comp., ῥᾷον φέρειν Thuc. III. Sup. ῥᾷστα, esp. in phrases, ῥᾷστα φέρειν Soph.; ὡς ῥᾷστα φέρειν Aesch.

ραδιουργεω.def: ῥᾳδιουργέω, (ῥαδιουργός) I. to do things with ease or off-hand, Luc. II. to live an easy, lazy life, take things easily, Xen. 2. to act thoughtlessly or recklessly, to do wrong, misbehave, id.

ραδιουργημα.def: ῥᾳδιούργημα, ατος, τό, (from ῥᾳδιουργέω) a reckless act, crime, Plut.

ραδιουργια.def: ῥᾳδιουργία, ἡ, I. ease in doing, facility, Xen. II. easiness, laziness, sloth, id. 2. recklessness, want of principle, wickedness, lewdness, id.: fraud, Plut.

ραδιουργοσ.def: ῥᾳδι-ουργός, όν (⁎ἔργω) 1. properly, doing things easily; in bad sense, unscrupulous, reckless, Arist. 2. of things, impure, Xen.

ραθαμιγξ.def: ῥᾰθ̆άμιγξ, ιγγος, I. a drop, Il., Hes. II. of solids, a grain, bit, Il. (deriv. uncertain)

ραθαπυγιζω.gloss: to give one a slap on the buttocks
ραθαπυγιζω.def: ῥᾰθᾰ-πῡγίζω, (ῥάσσω, πυγή) to give one a slap on the buttocks, Ar.

ραθυμεω.gloss: to leave off work, to be remiss
ραθυμεω.def: ῥᾳθυμέω to leave off work, to be remiss, Xen.

ραθυμια.gloss: easiness of temper, a taking things easily
ραθυμια.def: ῥᾳθῡμία, ἡ, I. easiness of temper, a taking things easily, Thuc. 2. recreation, relaxation, amusement, Eur. II. in bad sense, indifference, sluggishness, laziness, Xen., etc.; ῥ. κτήσασθαι to get a name for laziness, Eur. 2. heedlessness, rashness, Plat.

ραθυμοσ.gloss: taking things easy, indifferent, lazy, sluggish
ραθυμοσ.def: ῥᾴ-θῡμος, ον, I. taking things easy, indifferent, lazy, sluggish, Lat. socors, Soph., etc. II. of things, easy, Lat. securus, Isocr., Plat.:—adv. -μως, Plat. 2. adv. also, like ῥᾳδίως, lightly, with equanimity, id.; comp. -ότερον, Isocr.; -οτέρως, Arist.

ραιβοκρανοσ.def: ῥαιβό-κρᾱνος, ον, (κράνιον) with crooked head, Anth.

ραιβοσ.def: ῥαιβός, ή, όν crooked, bent, Arist.

ραιζω.gloss: to grow easier, find relief, recover from illness
ραιζω.def: ῥᾱΐζω, (ῥᾴδιος) to grow easier, find relief, recover from illness, Plat., Dem.:— to take one's rest, Xen.

ραινω.def: ῥαίνω I. to sprinkle, besprinkle, ῥάσσατε (sc. δῶμα ὕδατι) Od.; αἵματι βωμόν Eur.:—Pass., πύργοι αἵματι ἐρράδατ’ Il.; αἵματι δ’ ἐρράδαται τοῖχοι Od.:—of dust, ἵπποι ῥαίνοντο κονίηι Il. 2. metaph., ῥ. τινὰ ὕμνωι Pind. II. to sprinkle, with acc. of the thing sprinkled, ῥαίνειν ἐς τὰ βλέφαρα to sprinkle (vinegar) in their eyes, Ar.

ραιω.def: ῥαίω I. to break, shiver, shatter, wreck, Od.;— Pass., ῥαιόμενος one shipwrecked, id.; φάσγανον ἐρραίσθη was shivered, Il. II. to crush, destroy, in Pass., Aesch., Soph.

ρακα.def: ῥακά Hebr. word expressive of utter contempt, NTest.

ρακιον.def: ῥᾰ́κιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of ῥάκος) a rag, in pl. rags, Ar.

ρακιοσυρραπταδησ.def: ῥᾰκιο-συρραπτάδης, ου, ὁ, a rag-stitcher, Ar.

ρακοεισ.def: ῥᾰκόεις, εσσα, εν I. ragged, torn, tattered, Anth. II. wrinkled, id. (from ῥᾰ́κος)

ρακοσ.def: ῥᾰ́κος, ος, εος, τό, I. a ragged garment, a rag, Od., Ar.: in pl. ῥάκεα, attic ῥάκη, rags, tatters, Od., Hdt., etc. 2. generally, a strip of cloth, Hdt.: a strip of flesh, Aesch. II. in pl. rents in the face, wrinkles, Ar. III. metaph. a rag, remnant, Anon. ap. Arist.; of an old seaman, ἁλίοιο βίου ῥάκος Anth.

ρακοω.def: ῥᾰκόω, (from ῥᾰ́κος) to tear in strips, Plut.

ρακωμα.def: ῥάκωμα, ατος, τό, (from ῥᾰκόω) in pl., = ῥάκη, rags, Ar.

ραμφοσ.def: ῥάμφος, ος, εος, τό, a beak, bill, neb, Ar.

ρανισ.def: ῥᾰνίς, ίδος, ἡ, (ῥαίνω) a drop, Eur.; a rain-drop, Ar.

ραντηριοσ.def: ῥαντήριος, η, ον (ῥαίνω) of or for sprinkling:—in Aesch., it seems to be bedabbled, reeking.

ραντιζω.def: ῥαντίζω, I. = ῥαίνω, NTest. II. of the effect, to purify, id.

ραντισμοσ.def: ῥαντισμός, οῦ, ὁ, (from ῥαντίζω) a sprinkling, NTest.

ραξ.def: ῥάξ a grape, Lat. racemus, Plat.

ραπιζω.gloss: to strike with a stick, to cudgel, flog, bastinado
ραπιζω.def: ῥᾰπίζω, (ῥαπίς) I. to strike with a stick, to cudgel, flog, bastinado, Hdt., Dem. II. to slap in the face, NTest.

ραπισμα.gloss: a stroke, a slap on the face
ραπισμα.def: ῥάπισμα, ατος, τό, (ῥαπίζω) a stroke, a slap on the face, Luc.

ραπτοσ.def: ῥαπτός, ή, όν (ῥάπτω) I. stitched, patched, Od. 2. metaph. strung together, continuous, of verses, Pind. II. worked with the needle: ῥαπτόν, οῦ, an embroidered carpet, Xen.; ῥαπτὴ σφαῖρα a stitched ball, of divers colours, Anth.

ραπτω.def: ῥάπτω I. to sew or stitch together, stich, Il., Ar.:— Mid., ῥάπτεσθαι ὀχετὸν δερμάτων to make oneself a pipe of leather, Hdt.; ῥαψάμενος τουτί (sc. τὸ προσκεφάλαιον) having got it stitched, Ar.; but also, to sew on or to one, id.:—Pass., ἐρράφθαι τὸ χεῖλος to have one's lip sewed up, Dem. II. metaph. to devise, contrive, plot, Hom., etc.; proverb., τὸ ὑπόδημα ἔρραψας μὲν σύ, ὑπεδήσατο δὲ Ἀρισταγόρης you made the shoe, but Aristagoras put it on, Hdt.

ραριον.def: Ρ̓άριον (from Ρ̓ᾶρος) τὸ Ρ̓άριον (sc. πεδίον) the field of Rarus, sacred to Demeter, where tillage was first practised, Hhymn.

ραροσ.def: Ρ̓ᾶρος, ου, Raros, father of Triptolemus.

ραστωνευω.def: ῥᾳστωνεύω, (= ῥαθυμέω) to be idle, listless, Xen. (from ῥᾳστώνη)

ραστωνη.def: ῥᾳστώνη, ιονιξ ῥῃστώνη, ἡ, (ῥᾷστος) I. easiness or an easy way of doing anything, Plat.; ῥᾳστώνῃ or μετὰ ῥᾳστώνης with ease, easily, lightly, id.; ῥᾳστώνην φυγῆς παρέχειν to provide an easy way of escape, Plut. II. easiness of temper, good nature, kindness, Lat. facilitas, τινός to or towards a person, Hdt. III. relief or recovery from, τῆς πόσεως from the effects of drinking, Plat.: absol. rest leisure, ease, id.; διὰ ῥᾳστώνην for the sake of resting, Xen.: —also luxurious ease, indolence, carelessness, Thuc., Dem.

ραφανιδοω.gloss: to thrust a radish up the fundament
ραφανιδοω.def: ῥᾰφᾰνῑδόω, to thrust a radish up the fundament, a punishment of adulterers in Athens, Ar. (from ῥᾰφᾰνίς)

ραφανισ.def: ῥᾰφᾰνίς, ῖδος, the radish, Lat. raphanus, Ar.

ραφευσ.def: ῥᾰφεύς, έως, ὁ, (ῥάπτω) a stitcher, patcher: metaph., ῥ. φόνου a planner of murder, Aesch.

ραφη.def: ῥᾰφή, ἡ, (ῥάπτω) 1. a seam, Lat. sutura, Od. 2. the suture of the skull, Hdt.; so, ῥαφαὶ ὀστέων Eur.

ραφισ.def: ῥᾰφίς, δοριξ ῥαπίς, ίδος, ἡ, (ῥάπτω) a needle, Anth.

ραχια.gloss: the sea breaking on the shore
ραχια.def: ῥᾱχία, ιονιξ ῥηχίη, ἡ, (ῥήγνυμι, cf. ῥηγμίν) I. the sea breaking on the shore, esp. the flood-tide, opp. to ἄμπωτις, Hdt. II. a rocky shore or beach, Aesch., Thuc.

ραχιζω.gloss: to cut through the spine, to cleave in twain
ραχιζω.def: ῥᾰχίζω, to cut through the spine, to cleave in twain, Aesch., Soph. (from ῥᾰ́χις)

ραχισ.gloss: the lower part of the back, the chine
ραχισ.def: ῥάχις I. the lower part of the back, the chine, Il.: then, the spine or backbone, ὑπὸ ῥάχιν παγῆναι to be impaled, Aesch. II. anything ridged like the backbone, a mountain-ridge, Hdt.

ραχιωδησ.def: ῥᾱχι-ώδης, ες (ῥαχία, εἶδος) with surf, Strab.

ραχοσ.def: ῥᾱχός, ιονιξ ῥηχός, οῦ, a thorn-bush, briar, Xen.:— collectively, a thorn-hedge, a wattled fence, Hdt.

ραψωδεω.def: ῥαψῳδέω (ῥαψῳδός) 1. to recite epic poems, Plat. 2. in contemptuous sense, to repeat by heart or rote, to declaim, Dem., Luc.; c. inf. to keep saying that.., Dem.

ραψωδια.def: ῥαψῳδία, ἡ, (ῥαψῳδός) I. recitation of epic poetry, Plat. 2. epic composition, opp. to lyric (κιθαρῳδία), id. II. a portion of an epic poem fit for recitation at one time, e. g. a book of the Iliad or Odyssey, a lay, canto, Plut., Luc.

ραψωδικοσ.def: ῥαψῳδικός, ή, όν of or for a rhapsodist: ἡ -κή (with and without τέχνη), the rhapsodist's art, Plat. (from ῥαψῳδός)

ραψωδοσ.def: ῥαψ-ῳδός, οῦ, ὁ, (ῥάπτω, ᾠδή) I. properly one who stitches or strings songs together; esp. a person who recited epic poems, a rhapsodist, applied to Homer, Plat.; but ῥαψῳδοί commonly meant a class of persons who got their living by reciting the poems of Homer, Hdt., Plat.; v. ῥαψῳδία II. II. Soph. calls the Sphinx ῥαψῳδὸς κύων, because she proposed her riddle publicly, as the rhapsodists did their lays.

ρεα.def: Ῥέα Rhea, daughter of Uranus and Gaia, wife of Cronus, mother of the gods, Hom., etc.
ῥέα (= ῥεῖα) easily, lightly, Il. (Sometimes used as one long syll.)

ρεγκω.def: ῥέγκω, to snore, Lat. sterto, Aesch., Ar.; of horses, to snort, Eur. (Formed from the sound.)

ρεζω.def: ῥέζω I. to do, act, deal, Od.:—absol., Hom.:—c. acc. rei, to do, accomplish, make, id., etc.: —Pass., μῆχος ῥεχθέντος κακοῦ a remedy for mischief once done, Il. 2. c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, to do something to one, κακὸν ῥέζειν τινά Hom.; ἀγαθὰ ῥ. τινά id.; also more rarely c. dat. pers., μηκέτι μοι κακὰ ῥέζετε do me no more mischiefs, Od.; ὅσα βροτοῖς ἔρεξας κακά Eur. 3. with strengthd. signf., εἴ τι ῥέξει if it shall avail aught, be of any service, Il. II. in spec. sense, to perform sacrifices, Hom., Soph.; absol. to do sacrifice, Lat. operari, facere, ῥέζειν θεῶι Hom.:—sometimes with the victim in acc., ῥέξω βοῦν ἦνιν will sacrifice it, id.

ρεθοσ.def: ῥέθος, ος, εος, τό, I. a limb, in pl. the limbs, body, Il. II. in sg. the face, countenance, Soph., Eur.

ρεια.def: ῥεῖα (adverb of ῥᾴδιος) easily, lightly, Hom.; θεοὶ ῥεῖα ζώοντες the gods who live at ease, Lat. securum agentes aevom, id.; strengthd. ῥεῖα μάλ’ Il.

ρειθρον.gloss: that which flows, a river, stream
ρειθρον.def: ῥεῖθρον, ου, τό, (ῥέω) I. that which flows, a river, stream, mostly in pl., ποταμοῖο ῥέεθρα Il.; Στυγὸς ὕδατος αἰπὰ ῥ. id.; streams of blood, Aesch.:—sg., Hdt., Aesch. II. the bed or channel of a river, Il., Hdt.

ρεκτηρ.def: ῥεκτηφαιλινγ ον λεμβυφ [] (ῥέζω) a worker, doer, Hes.

ρεκτησ.def: ῥέκτης, ου, ὁ, (= ῥεκτήρ) active, Plut.

ρεμβομαι.def: ῥέμβομαι, Dep. to roam, rove, roll about, Plut.: metaph. to be unsteady, act at random, id.

ρεοσ.def: ῥέος, εος, τό, (ῥέω) (= ῥεῦμα) a stream, Aesch.

ρεπω.gloss: to incline downwards, to sink, fall
ρεπω.def: ῥέπω 1. properly of the descending scale, to incline downwards, to sink, fall, Lat. vergere, inclinare, Il., Ar.:—of things, to incline one way or the other, to be always shifting, Pind.; ὕπνος ἐπὶ βλεφάροις ῥέπων sleep falling upon the eyes, id. 2. of one of two contending parties, to preponderate, prevail, Hdt., Plat. 3. of persons, εὖ ῥέπει θεός is favourably inclined, Aesch.; ῥέπειν ἐπί τι to incline towards a thing, Dem.; εἴς or πρός τι Plat., Arist.; εἴς τινα Luc. 4. of duties, ῥ. εἴς τινα to fall or devolve upon one, Aesch., Soph. 5. of events, to fall, happen in a certain way, Soph.; r(. εἴς τι to turn or come to something, Aesch., Ar.

ρευμα.gloss: that which flows, a flow, stream, current
ρευμα.def: ῥεῦμα, ατος, τό, (ῥέω) I. that which flows, a flow, stream, current, Aesch., Soph., etc. 2. the stream of a river, mostly in pl., Hdt., Eur.; a stream of lava, Thuc.: metaph. a stream or flood of men, Trag., Soph. 3. a flood, Thuc. II. a discharge from the body, a flux, rheum, Luc.

ρευματιζομαι.def: ῥευμᾰτίζομαι, (from ῥεῦμα) Pass. to flow as a current, Strab.

ρευματιον.def: ῥευμάτιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of ῥεῦμα) a rivulet, Plut.

ρευστικοσ.def: ῥευστικός, ή, όν (ῥέω) flowing, liquid, Plut.

ρεω.def: ῥέω I. to flow, run, stream, gush, Hom., etc.:—with dat. of that which flows, πηγὴ ῥέει ὕδατι the fountain runs with water, Il.; ῥέεν αἵματι γαῖα id.; ῥεῖ γάλακτι πέδον Eur.; of a river, μέγας ῥεῖ runs with full stream, Hdt.; so, πολὺς ῥεῖ, metaph. of men, Aesch.; of a river, also, ῥ. ἀπὸ χιόνος to derive its stream from melted snow, Hdt.:—proverb., ἄνω ῥέειν to flow backwards, of impossibilities, Eur. 2. metaph. of things, ἐκ χειρῶν βέλεα ῥέον from their hands rained darts, Il.; of a flow of words, ἀπὸ γλώσσης μέλιτος γλυκίων ῥέεν αὐδή id.; absol., of the tongue, to run glibly, Aesch. (cf. Hor., salso multoque fluenti): of words or sentiments, to be current, Soph. 3. to fall, drop off, e. g. of hair, Od., Theocr.: then, generally, to flow or melt away, perish, Soph., Plat. 4. of persons, ῥ. ἐπί or εἴς τι to be inclined, given to a thing, Isocr., Plat. II. very rarely trans. to let flow, pour, ἔρρει χοάς Eur. 2. c. acc. cogn., ῥείτω γάλα, μέλι let the land run milk, honey, Theocr.; οἶνον ῥέων Luc.

ρηγμα.def: ῥῆγμα, ατος, τό, (ῥήγνυμι) a breakage, fracture, Dem.

ρηγμιν.gloss: the sea breaking on the beach, the line of breakers, surf
ρηγμιν.def: ῥηγμίν, ορ -μίς, ῖνος, ὁ, the sea breaking on the beach, the line of breakers, surf, Hom.; ἐπὶ or παρὰ ῥηγμῖνι θαλάσσης by the edge of the sea, id.

ρηγνυμι.def: ῥήγνυμι I. to break, break asunder or in pieces, rend, shiver, shatter, Hom., etc.:—to rend garments, in sign of grief, Aesch.:—Mid. to break for oneself, get broken, Il. 2. to break a line of battle or body of men, id., Hdt.; in Mid., ῥήξασθαι φάλαγγας, στίχας to break oneself a way through the lines, Il.; absol., ῥήξασθαι to break or force one's way, id. 3. to let break loose, let loose, id. 4. ῥῆξαι φωνήν to let loose the voice, of children and persons who have been dumb breaking into speech, Hdt.: then to speak freely, speak out (like rumpere vocem, Virgil), id., Ar., etc. 5. δακρύων ῥήξασα νάματα having let loose floods of tears, Soph.; so, ῥ. κλαυθμόν Plut. II. absol. in the form ῥήσσω, to beat the ground, dance, Il. III. later, as a term of fighters, to fell, knock down, Dem. B. Pass., mostly used in aor2 ἐρράγην [α], to break, burst, of waves, Il.; of clouds, Ar. 2. to break asunder, be rent, of the earth in an earthquake, Plat.; of garments, Xen. 3. to burst forth, like lightning, Ar. 4. of ships, to be wrecked, Dem.: metaph. of hopes, Aesch. C. intr., like Pass., to break forth, of a river, to break its bounds, Hdt.:—metaph. of sudden misfortunes, bursts of passion, Soph. II. in this intr. sense the perf. ἔρρωγα is commonly used of tears, id.; metaph., κακῶν πέλαγος ἔρρωγεν Aesch., etc.

ρηγοσ.def: ῥῆγος, ος, εος, τό, a rug, blanket, used as the covering of a bed or seat, Hom.; or as a garment, Od.

ρηκτοσ.def: ῥηκτός, ή, όν (ῥήγνυμι) that can be broken or rent, penetrable, Il.

ρημα.def: ῥῆμα, ατος, τό, (ῥέω, ἐρῶ) I. that which is said or spoken, a word, saying, Theogn., Hdt., etc.; κατὰ ῥῆμα word for word, Aeschin. 2. a phrase, opp. to ὄνομα (a single word), Plat. 3. the subject of speech, a thing, NTest. II. in Gramm., a verb, opp. to ὄνομα (a noun), ῥήματα καὶ ὀνόματα Plat.

ρηματιον.def: ῥημάτιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of ῥῆμα) a pet phrase, phrasicle, Ar.

ρηνοφορευσ.def: ῥηνο-φορεύς, έως, ὁ, (from ῥήν) (φέρω) clad in sheepskin, Anth.

ρηξηνορια.gloss: might to break through armed ranks
ρηξηνορια.def: ῥηξηνορία, ἡ, might to break through armed ranks Od. (from ῥηξήνωρ)

ρηξηνωρ.def: ῥηξ-ήνωρ, ορος, ὁ, (ῥήγνυμι, ἀνήρ) breaking through armed ranks, Hom.

ρηξικελευθοσ.def: ῥηξῐ-κέλευθος, ον, opening a path, of Apollo, Anth.

ρηξινουσ.def: ῥηξί-νους, ουν, breaking the spirit, of Bacchus, Anth.

ρηξισ.def: ῥῆξις, εως, (ῥήγνυμαι) a breaking, bursting, ῥήξεις broken flames, a bad omen, Eur.

ρησισ.def: ῥῆσις, εως, (Ῥέω, ἐρῶ) I. a saying, speaking, speech, Od., Hdt., etc.; ἡ ἀπὸ Σκυθῶν ῥῆσις the Scythian phrase, Hdt. 2. a resolution, declaration, id. II. a tale, legend, Pind. III. a phrase or passage, a speech in a play, Ar.

ρητεοσ.def: ῥητέος, ον, (verb. adj.) one must mention, Plat.

ρητηρ.def: ῥητηφαιλινγ ον λεμβυφ [] (Ῥέω, ἐρῶ) a speaker, Il.

ρητορεια.gloss: skill in public speaking, eloquence, oratory, rhetoric
ρητορεια.def: ῥητορεία, ἡ, I. skill in public speaking, eloquence, oratory, rhetoric, Plat. II. a piece of oratory, set speech, Isocr. (from ῥητορεύω)

ρητορευω.gloss: to speak in public, to use
ρητορευω.def: ῥητορεύω, (ῥήτωρ) I. to speak in public, to use or practise oratory, Plat.:—Pass., of the speech, to be spoken, Isocr. II. to teach oratory, Strab.

ρητορικοσ.def: ῥητορικός, ή, όν (ῥήτωρ) 1. oratorical, rhetorical, ἡ ῥητορική (sc. τέχνη) rhetoric, the art of speaking, Plat.; ῥητορικὴ δειλία an orator's timidity, Aeschin.:— adv. -κῶς, Plat. 2. of persons, skilled in speaking, fit to be an orator, id., etc.

ρητοσ.def: ῥητός, ή, όν (verb. adj. of ⁎ῥέω, ἐρῶ) I. stated, specified, Il.; ἐς χρόνον ῥητόν at a set or stated time, Hdt.; ἡμέραι ῥ. Thuc.; ἐπὶ ῥητοῖς γέρασι with fixed prerogatives, id.; ῥ. ἀργύριον a stated sum, id.; ἐπὶ ῥητοῖς on stated terms, on certain conditions, Hdt., Eur.:—adv. ῥητῶς, expressly, distinctly, NTest. 2. spoken of, known, famous, Hes. II. that may be spoken or told, Aesch., Soph.; ῥητὸν ἄρρητόν τ’ ἔπος, Lat. fas nefasque, Soph. III. in Mathem., ῥητά are rational quantities, opp. to surds (ἄλογα), Plat.

ρητρα.def: ῥήτρα, ἡ, (Ῥέω, ἐρῶ) I. a verbal agreement, bargain, covenant, Od.; παρὰ τὴν ῥήτραν Xen. II. the unwritten laws of Lycurgus were called ῥῆτραι, Lex ap. Plut.: generally, a decree, ordinance, Tyrtae., Xen. III. speech, a word, Luc.

ρητωρ.def: ῥήτωρ (ἐρέω, ἐρῶ) a public speaker, pleader, Lat. orator, Eur., etc.

ριγεδανοσ.gloss: making one shudder with cold, chilling
ριγεδανοσ.def: ῥῑγεδᾰνός, ή, όν making one shudder with cold, chilling: metaph., ῥιγεδανὴ Ἑλένη Helen at whose name one shudders, horrible, Il. (from ῥιγέω)

ριγεω.def: ῥιγέω (ῥῖγος) (note ἐρρίγοντι for ἐρριγότι.) I. to shiver or shudder with cold: metaph. to shudder with fear or horror, Il., Soph.:—c. inf. to shudder to do, shrink from doing, Il.; also, ῥ. μὴ.., Od. 2. to cool or slacken in zeal, Pind. 3. to bristle with arms, Theocr. II. trans. to shudder at anything, Il.

ριγηλοσ.def: ῥῑγηλός, ή, όν making to shiver, chilling, Hes.

ριγιον.def: ῥίγιον (neut. comp. adj. formed from ῥῖγος) more frosty, colder, Od.:—metaph. more horrible, Hom.

ριγιστοσ.def: ῥίγιστος, η, ον (Sup. adj. formed from ῥῖγος (as κῦ́διστος from κῦδος）) coldest: most horrible, Il.

ριγομαχησ.def: ῥῑγο-μάχης, ορ -χος, ου, (μάχομαι) fighting with cold, Anth.

ριγοσ.def: ῥῖγος, ος, εος, τό, frost, cold, Lat. frigus, Od., etc.

ριγοω.gloss: to be cold, shiver from cold
ριγοω.def: ῥιγόω (this word, like ἱδρόω, has an irreg. contr. into ω, ωι, for ου, οι,) to be cold, shiver from cold, Od., Hdt.

ριζα.def: ῥίζα, ης, ἡ, I. a root, Od., attic: in pl. the roots, Hom. 2. metaph. the roots of the eye, Od.; the roots or foundations of the earth, Hes., Aesch., etc. 3. ἐκ ῥιζῶν, Lat. radicitus, Plut. II. anything that grows like a root from one stem, whence Pindar calls Libya the τρίτη ῥίζα χθονός, considering the earth as divided into three continents. III. metaph. the root or stock from which a family springs, Lat. stirps, Pind., Aesch., etc.; and so a race, family, Aesch., Eur., etc.

ριζιον.def: ῥιζίον, ου, τό, (Dim. of ῥίζα) a little root, Ar.

ριζοβολεω.def: ῥιζοβολέω, to strike root, Anth. (from ῥιζοβόλος)

ριζοθεν.def: ῥιζόθεν (ῥίζα) by, from the roots, Luc.

ριζοτομοσ.def: ῥιζο-τόμος, ὁ, (τέμνω) one who cuts roots, Luc.

ριζοφαγεω.def: ῥιζοφᾰγέω, to eat roots, Strab.; ῥ. τὰ σπέρματα to destroy them by nibbling the roots, id. (from ῥιζοφᾰ́γος)

ριζοω.def: ῥιζόω, (ῥίζα) I. to make to strike root: metaph. to root in the ground, plant, Od.; ἐρρίζωσε τὴν τυραννίδα Hdt.: —Pass. to take root, strike root, Xen.: metaph. to be rooted, firmly fixed, Soph., NTest. II. Pass. also of land, to be planted with trees, Od.

ριζωμα.def: ῥίζωμα, ατος, τό, (from ῥιζόω) a root: metaph. a stem, race Aesch.

ριζωρυχοσ.def: ῥιζ-ωρύχος, ον, root-grubbing, of grammarians, Anth.

ριζωσισ.def: ῥίζωσις, εως, a taking root, beginning life, Plut.

ρικνοσ.def: ῥικνός, ή, όν shrivelled with cold: generally, shrivelled, crooked, Hhymn., Anth.

ριμφα.def: ῥίμφα (ῥίπτω) adv. lightly, swiftly, fleetly, Il., Aesch.

ριμφαρματοσ.def: ῥιμφ-άρμᾰτος, ον, (ἅρμα) of a swift chariot, Pind.; ῥ. ἁμίλλαις with the swift racing of chariots, Soph.

ρινεγκαταπηξιγενειοσ.gloss: with a nose reaching to the chin
ρινεγκαταπηξιγενειοσ.def: ῥῑν-εγκᾰτᾰπηξῐ-γένειος, ον, (ῥίς, ἐγκαταπήγνυμι) with a nose reaching to the chin, Anth.

ρινη.def: ῥῑ́νη, ἡ, a file or rasp, Xen.

ρινηλατεω.def: ῥῑνηλᾰτέω, to track by scent, Aesch. (from ῥῑνηλάτης)

ρινηλατησ.def: ῥῑν-ηλάτης, ου, ὁ, (ἐλαύνω) one who tracks by scent, of hounds.

ρινοβολοσ.def: ῥῑνό-βολος, ον, (βάλλω) emitted through the nose, of a snorting sound, Anth.

ρινοκερωσ.def: ῥῑνό-κερως, ωτος, ὁ, (ῥίς, κέρας) the rhinoceros or nosehorn, Strab.

ρινον.def: ῥῑνόν, οῦ, (= ῥινός II. 1) 1. a hide, Il. 2. = ῥινός II. 2, a shield, Od.

ρινοσ.def: ῥῑνός, οῦ, I. the skin of a man, Hom. II. the hide of a beast, esp. an ox-hide, id. 2. an ox-hide shield, id.

ρινουχοσ.def: ῥιν-οῦχος, ὁ, (ῥίς II) a sewer, Lat. cloaca, Strab.

ριον.def: ῥίον, ου, τό, 1. any jutting part of a mountain, 1. the peak, Hom. 2. a headland, foreland, Od., Thuc.

ριπη.def: ῥῑπή, ἡ, (ῥίπτω) 1. the swing or force with which anything is thrown, Lat. impetus, αἰγανέης ῥιπή the flight of a javelin, Il.; ῥιπὴ Βορέαο the sweep or rush of the N. wind, id.; ῥιπὴ Διόθεν, of a storm, Aesch.; ἐννυχιᾶν ἀπὸ ῥιπᾶν prob. means from the quarter of the night storms, i.e. from the North, Soph.; ῥ. πυρός the rush of fire, Il. 2. ῥ. πτερύγων a flapping of wings, Aesch.; of the buzz of a gnat's wing, id.; of quivering light, ῥιπαὶ ἄστρων Soph.; of any rapid movement, ῥ. ποδῶν Eur.; ἐν ῥιπῇ ὀφθαλμοῦ in the twinkling of an eye, NTest.

ριπιζω.def: ῥῑπίζω, (ῥιπίς) to fan the flame, Lat. conflare, Ar.:—Pass. to be blown about, NTest.

ριπισ.gloss: a fan for raising the fire
ριπισ.def: ῥῑπίς, ίδος, ἡ, (ῥίψ) I. a fan for raising the fire, Ar. II. a lady's fan, Anth.

ριπταζω.gloss: to throw to and fro, toss about
ριπταζω.def: ῥιπτάζω, (Frequentative of ῥίπτω) to throw to and fro, toss about, Lat. jactare, Il.; ὀφρύσι ῥιπτάζειν to move the eyebrows up and down, Hhymn.:—Pass. to be tossed about, Plut.

ριπτοσ.def: ῥιπτός, ή, όν (verb. adj. of ῥίπτω) thrown, ῥ.μόρος death by being thrown down (a precipice), Soph.

ριπτω.def: ῥίπτω I. to throw, cast, hurl, Hom., etc.; ῥ. χθονί to throw on the ground, Soph.:— to cast a net, Pass., ἔρριπται ὁ βόλος the cast has been made, Orac. ap. Hdt.:— to throw or toss about, πλοκάμους Eur. II. to cast out of house or land, Soph.:— Pass., μὴ ῥιφθῶ κυσίν id. III. to throw off or away, of arms, clothes, Eur., etc. IV. ῥ. λόγους to cast them forth, hurl them, Aesch., Eur.:—but also, to throw them away, waste them, Aesch., Eur.: Pass., οἴχεται ταῦτ’ ἐρριμμένα Soph. V. to cast lots or dice, Eur., Plat. VI. ῥ. ἑαυτόν to throw or cast oneself down, Xen.;—then absol. to fling oneself, ἐς πόντον Theogn.; ἐς τάφρον Eur.

ρισ.def: ῥίς, ίδος, ἡ, I. the nose, Lat. nasus, Hom., Hdt., etc. 2. in pl. the nostrils, nose, Lat. nares, Il., etc. II. a pipe or conduit.

ριψ.def: ῥίψ plaited work, wicker-work, a mat, Lat. crates, Od., etc.

ριψασπισ.gloss: throwing away his shield in battle, a recreant
ριψασπισ.def: ῥίψ-ασπις, ιδος, ὁ, ἡ, throwing away his shield in battle, a recreant, Ar.

ριψισ.def: ῥῖψις, εως, I. a throwing, casting, hurling, Plat. 2. a casting about of the eyes, Plut. II. a being thrown or hurled, Plat.

ριψοκινδυνοσ.def: ῥιψο-κίνδῡνος, ον, running needless risks, fool-hardy, reckless, Xen.

ριψοπλοσ.def: ῥίψ-οπλος, ον, throwing away one's arms, Aesch.

ροα.def: ῥόᾱ, ἡ, I. ionic and epic ῥοιή, a pomegranate-tree, Od. II. the fruit, a pomegranate, Hhymn., Ar. 2. a knob shaped like a pomegranate, Hdt.

ροδανη.def: ῥοδᾰ́νη, ἡ, the woof or weft, Batr. (from ῥοδᾰνός)

ροδανοσ.def: ῥοδᾰνός, ή, όν waving, flickering, Il. (deriv. uncertain)

ροδεοσ.def: ῥόδεος (ῥόδον) I. of roses, Eur. II. like a rose, rosy, Anth.

ροδιακοσ.def: Ῥοδιακός, ή, όν (Ῥόδος) Rhodian, of Rhodes, Strab.: —also Ῥόδιος, η, ον, Il., Xen.

ροδοδακτυλοσ.def: ῥοδο-δάκτῠλος, ον, rosy-fingered, of Aurora, Hom.

ροδοεισ.def: ῥοδόεις, εσσα, εν (ῥόδον) I. of roses, Il., Eur. II. rose-coloured, Anth.

ροδομηλον.def: ῥοδό-μηλον, δοριξ ῥοδό-μᾱλον, ου, τό, a rose-apple: metaph. of a rosy cheek, Theocr.

ροδον.def: ῥόδον, ου, τό, the rose, Lat. rosa, Hhymn., Theogn., etc.; aeolic βρόδον, Sapph.:—metaph., ῥόδα μ’ εἴρηκας you've spoken roses of me, have said all things sweet and lovely, Ar.

ροδοπηχυσ.def: ῥοδό-πηχυς, δοριξ ῥοδό-πᾱχυς, υ, rosy-armed, Hhymn., Hes., etc.

ροδοσ.def: Ῥόδος, ου, the isle of Rhodes, Il., etc.

ροδοχρωσ.def: ῥοδό-χρως, ωτος, ὁ, ἡ, (= ῥοδόπηχυς, Theocr.)

ροδωνια.def: ῥοδωνιά, ἡ, (ῥόδον) a rose-bed, garden of roses, Lat. rosarium, Dem., etc.

ροη.def: ῥοή, ἡ, (ῥέω) a river, stream, flood, Hom., etc.; mostly in pl., ἐπ’ Ὠκεανοῖο ῥοάων Il.; ἀμπέλου ῥοαί the juice of the grape, Eur.:—metaph. the stream of song or poesy, Pind.; also, ῥοαί the tide of affairs, id.

ροθεω.gloss: to make a rushing noise, to dash
ροθεω.def: ῥοθέω, (ῥόθος) to make a rushing noise, to dash, of waves or the stroke of oars: hence, of any confused noise, ταῦτα ἐρρόθουν ἐμοί such clamours they raised against me, Soph.; λόγοι ἐρρόθουν there was a noise of words, id.

ροθιαζω.def: ῥοθιάζω, (strengthd. form of ῥοθέω) of pigs, to make a guttling noise, Ar.

ροθιασ.def: ῥοθιάς, άδος, dashing, Aesch. (poet. fem. of ῥόθιος)

ροθιοσ.def: ῥόθιος, ον, (ῥόθος) I. rushing, roaring, dashing, of waves, Od.; of oars, Eur. II. as Subst. ῥόθια, τά, waves dashing on the beach, breakers, waves, Soph., etc.;—collectively in sg. the surf, surge, Aesch., Eur. 2. a shout of applause, Ar.; generally, a tumult, riot, Eur.

ροθοσ.gloss: a rushing noise, dash of waves
ροθοσ.def: ῥόθος, ὁ, 1. a rushing noise, dash of waves or of oars, ἐξ ἑνὸς ῥόθου with one stroke, i. e. all at once, Aesch. 2. of any confused, inarticulate sound, Περσίδος γλώσσης ῥ. the noise of the Persian (i. e. barbarian) tongue, id. (Formed from the sound.)

ροια.def: ῥοιά, ἡ, (later attic for ῥοά) mulberry.

ροιβδεω.gloss: to swallow with a noise, suck down
ροιβδεω.def: ῥοιβδέω I. to swallow with a noise, suck down, of Charybdis, Od.; cf. ἀναρροιβδέω. II. like ῥοιζέω, to move with a rustling sound, make to rustle, Aesch.

ροιβδησισ.def: ῥοίβδησις, εως, a whistling, piping, Eur.

ροιβδοσ.def: ῥοῖβδος, ὁ, any rushing noise, πτερῶν ῥ. the whirring of wings, Soph.; ἀνέμου ῥ. whistling of the wind, Ar. (Formed from the sound.)

ροιζεω.def: ῥοιζέω, (ῥοῖζος) to whistle, Lat. stridere, Il.; of a snake, to hiss, Hes.:—Pass. to rush through the air, ἐρροίζητο (3rd sg. plup.) Anth.

ροιζημα.def: ῥοίζημα, ατος, τό, (from ῥοιζέω) a rushing, whirring noise or motion, as of birds, Ar.

ροιζοσ.def: ῥοῖζος, ὁ, ιονιξ ἡ, I. the whistling or whizzing of an arrow, Il.:—any whistling or piping sound, as of a shepherd, Od. II. rushing motion, a rush, swing, Plut. (Formed from the sound.)

ρομβητοσ.def: ῥομβητός, ή, όν spun round like a top, Anth.

ρομβοειδησ.def: ῥομβο-ειδής, ές (εἶδος) rhomboidal, Strab.; ῥ. σχῆμα a rhomboid, a four-sided figure with the opposite sides and angles equal.

ρομβοσ.def: ῥόμβος, ορ ῥύμβος, ὁ, (ῥέμβω) I. a spinning-top or wheel, Lat. turbo, Eur., Anth. 2. a magic wheel, used by sorcerers to aid their spells, Theocr., Hor. II. a spinning, whirling motion, of a top or wheel, ἱέντα ῥόμβον ἀκόντων shooting forth whirling darts, Pind.; ῥ. αἰετοῦ the eagle's swoop, id. III. a rhomb, lozenge, i. e. a four-sided figure with all the sides, but only the opposite angles, equal, Euclid. 2. a fish, the turbot, brill.

ρομβωτοσ.def: ῥομβωτός, ή, όν (verb. adj.) (ῥόμβος III) lozenge-shaped, Anth.

ρομφαια.def: ῥομφαία, ἡ, a large sword, scymitar, used by the Thracians, Plut., NTest. (Foreign word.)

ροοσ.def: ῥόος, ου, (ῥέω) a stream, flow, current, Hom., etc.; ποταμοὺς ἔτρεψε νέεσθαι κὰρ ῥόον to flow in their own bed, Il.; κατὰ ῥόον down stream, Od., Hdt., etc.; πρὸς ῥόον against stream, Il.:— a current at sea, Thuc.

ροπαλον.def: ῥόπᾰλον, ου, τό, (ῥέπω) I. a club, cudgel, thicker at the buttend; used to cudgel an ass, Il.; to walk with, Od., etc.:— a war-club or mace, shod with metal, id., Hdt. II. = ῥόπτρον III, Xen.

ροπη.gloss: inclination downwards, the sinking of the scale
ροπη.def: ῥοπή, ἡ, (ῥέπω) I. inclination downwards, the sinking of the scale, Aesch.; διαφέρειν τὴν ῥ. to disturb the balance, Plut. 2. metaph. the turn of the scale, the critical moment, Lat. momentum, ἔχεται ῥοπᾶς (sc. ἡ πόλις) is at a crisis of her fortunes, Alcae. ap. Ar.; ῥ. Δίκας the balance or critical turn of Justice, Aesch.; σμικρὰ παλαιὰ σώματ’ εὐνάζει ῥοπή a slight turn of the scale lays aged bodies to rest, Soph.; ἐπὶ σμικρᾶς ῥοπῆς dependent on a slight turn of the scale, of one dying, Eur.; ἐπὶ ῥοπῆς μιᾶς ὄντες depending on a single turn of the scale, Thuc.; ῥ. βίου the turning point of life, i. e. death, Soph. II. metaph. influence, Dem.

ροπτρον.def: ῥόπτρον, ου, τό, (ῥέπω) I. the wood in a mouse-trap which springs up when touched, Archil.; metaph., δίκης ῥόπτρον Eur. II. a tambourine or kettledrum, Luc., Anth. III. the knocker on a housedoor, Eur.

ρουσιοσ.def: ῥούσιος, ον, reddish, Lat. russus, Anth.

ροφεω.gloss: to sup greedily up, gulp down
ροφεω.def: ῥοφέω 1. to sup greedily up, gulp down, Aesch., Ar. 2. to drain dry, empty, Ar.; so, ῥ. ἀρτηρίας, of the poison on the robe of Hercules, Soph.

ροφητικοσ.def: ῥοφητικός, ή, όν (from ῥοφέω) drawing in, absorbing, Strab.

ροφητοσ.def: ῥοφητός, ή, όν (from ῥοφέω) that can be or is supped up, Strab.

ροχθεω.gloss: to dash with a roaring sound
ροχθεω.def: ῥοχθέω, to dash with a roaring sound, of the sea, Od. (from ῥόχθος)

ροχθοσ.def: ῥόχθος, ὁ, a roaring of the sea.

ροωδησ.def: ῥο-ώδης, ες (εἶδος) with a strong stream, of a sea in which there are strong currents, Thuc.: of rocks, exposed to such seas, Strab.

ρυαξ.def: ῥύαξ, ᾱκος, (ῥέω) a rushing stream, a torrent, Thuc.; ὁ ῥ. τοῦ πυρός, of a stream of lava, id.

ρυγχιον.def: ῥυγχίον, ου, τό, (Dim. of ῥύγχος, Ar.)

ρυγχοσ.def: ῥύγχος, ος, εος, τό, (ῥύζω) a snout, muzzle, of swine, Stesich.; of dogs, Theocr.: of birds, a beak, neb, Ar.

ρυζω.def: ῥύζω, to growl, snarl, ῥύζει ἐπίκλαυτον νόμον snarls its melancholy ditty, Ar. (Formed from the sound.)

ρυθμιζω.def: ῥυθμίζω, (ῥυθμός) to bring into measure or proportion: generally, to order, to educate, train, Xen., etc.:—metaph., ῥ. λύπην ὅπου to define the place of grief, Soph.:—Mid., ῥ. πλόκαμον to arrange one's hair, Eur.:—Pass., νηλεῶς ὧδ’ ἐρρύθμισμαι thus ruthlessly am I brought to order, Aesch.

ρυθμοσ.def: ῥυθμός, ιονιξ ῥυσμός, οῦ, ὁ, (ῥέω) I. measured motion, time, rhythm, Lat. numerus, Ar., Plat., etc.: —ἐν ῥυθμῷ in time, Virgil's in numerum, Xen.; μετὰ ῥυθμοῦ Thuc.; θάττονα ῥυθμὸν ἐπάγειν to play in quicker time, Xen. II. proportion or symmetry of parts, Plat. III. generally, arrangement, order, Eur. IV. the state or condition of the soul, temper, disposition, Theogn., etc. V. the form or shape of a thing, Hdt.; of a breastplate, Xen. VI. the wise, manner or fashion of a thing, Eur.; τίς ῥ. φόνου; what kind of slaughter? id.

ρυκανη.def: ῥῠκᾰ́νη, ἡ, a plane, Anth. (deriv. uncertain)

ρυμα.def: ῥῦμα, ατος, τό, (⁎ῥύω ἐρύω) I. that which is drawn: 1. τόξου ῥῦμα, i. e. the Persian archers, opp. to λόγχης ἰσχύς, i. e. the Greek spearmen, Aesch.; ἐκ τόξου ῥύματος from the distance of a bow- shot, Xen. 2. a towing-line, Polyb. II. （ῥύομαι) a defence, protection, Eur.; πύργου ῥ. a tower of defence, Soph.

ρυμη.def: ῥύμη, ἡ, (⁎ῥύω ἐρύω) 1. the force, swing, rush of a body in motion, Lat. impetus, ῥύμῃ with a swing, Thuc.; πτερύγων ῥύμη the rush of wings, Ar.; ἡ ῥ. τῶν ἵππων Xen.:—metaph., εὐτυχεῖ ῥύμῃ θεοῦ Eur.; ἡ ῥ. τῆς ὀργῆς the vehemence of passion, Dem. 2. absol. a rush, charge, of soldiers, Thuc., Xen. a street, Lat. vicus, Polyb., NTest.

ρυμμα.def: ῥύμμα, ατος, τό, (ῥύπτω) anything for washing, soap, Plat.

ρυμοσ.def: ῥῡμός, οῦ, ὁ, (⁎ῥύω ἐρύω) the pole of a carriage, Il., Hdt.; ἐν πρώτῳ ῥυμῷ at the end of the pole, Il.

ρυμουλκεω.def: ῥῡμ-ουλκέω, (ῥῦμα I. 2, ἕλκω) to tow, Polyb., etc.

ρυομαι.def: ῥύομαι I. to draw to oneself, i. e. draw out of danger, to rescue, save, deliver, Hom., Hes., etc.; ῥ. τινα ὑπὲκ θανάτου, ὑπὲκ κακοῦ to save from.., Hom.;—so c. gen., ῥ. τινα τοῦ μὴ κατακαυθῆναι Hdt.; or c. inf. alone, ῥ. τινα θανεῖν or μὴ κατθανεῖν Eur.: also, to save from an illness, cure, Hdt.: to set free, redeem, Il.; ἐκ δουλοσύνης Hdt. II. generally, to shield, guard, protect, of guardian gods, chiefs, etc., Il. etc.:—of defensive armour, id. 2. Soph. has ῥῦσαι in a double sense, ῥῦσαι σεαυτὸν.., ῥῦσαι δὲ μίασμα τοῦ τεθνηκότος deliver thyself,—and deliver us from the pollution; so, ῥ. τὰς αἰτίας to remove the charges, Thuc. III. to draw back, to hold back, check, Od., Pind. IV. to keep off, Pind.

ρυπαινω.def: ῥῠπαίνω, (ῥύπος) to defile, disfigure, disparage, Arist.:—Pass. to be or become foul, Xen.

ρυπαρια.def: ῥῠπᾰρία, ἡ, dirt, filth: sordidness, Critias, Plut.

ρυπαροσ.def: ῥῠπᾰρός, ή, όν (ῥύσιος) foul, filthy, dirty:—metaph. dirty, sordid, Arist.:—adv. -ρῶς, Anth.

ρυπαω.def: ῥυπάω (ῥύπος) to be foul, filthy, dirty, Od.; imperf. ἐρρύπων, Ar.

ρυποομαι.def: ῥῠπόομαι, Pass. to be foul, perf. part. ῥερῠπωμένος, epic for ἐρρυπωμένοι, fouled, soiled, Od. (from ῥῠ́πος)

ρυποσ.def: ῥῠ́πος, ὁ, dirt, filth, dirtiness, uncleanness, heterocl. pl. ῥύπα, Od.; in sg., Plat., etc.

ρυππαπαι.def: ῥυππαπαί a cry of the Athenian rowers, like ὠόπ, yoho! Ar.; hence, τὸ ῥυππαπαί one's messmates, id.

ρυπτω.def: ῥύπτω (ῥύπος) to remove dirt from garments, to wash, Arist.:—Pass. to wash oneself, ἐξ ὅτου ἐγὼ ῥύπτομαι ever since I began to wash, i. e. from childhood, Ar.

ρυσαινομαι.def: ῥῡσαίνομαι, (ῥυσός) Pass. to be wrinkled, Anth.

ρυσιαζω.gloss: to seize as a pledge, to drag away
ρυσιαζω.def: ῥῡσῐάζω, (ῥύσιον) to seize as a pledge, to drag away, Eur.:—Pass. to be so dragged away, id.

ρυσιδιφροσ.def: ῥῡσί-διφρος, ον, preserving the chariot, Pind.

ρυσιον.def: ῥῡ́σιον, ου, τό, (ῥύομαι) that which is dragged away: I. booty, prey, ῥύσια ἐλαύνεσθαι, of cattle, Il.; τοῦ ῥυσίου θ’ ἥμαρτε, i. e. Helen., Aesch. II. that which is seized as a pledge, a pledge, surety, ῥύσια δοῦναι Solon.; ῥύσιον τιθέναι Soph. III. that which is seized by way of reprisal, φόνον φόνου ῥύσιον τῖσαι to suffer death in reprisal for death, id. IV. in pl. offerings for deliverance, Anth.

ρυσιοσ.def: ῥύσιος, ον, (ῥύομαι) delivering, saving, Aesch., Anth.

ρυσιπολισ.def: ῥῡσί-πολις, εως, saving the city, Aesch.

ρυσιπονοσ.def: ῥῡσί-πονος, ον, setting free from trouble, Anth.

ρυσισ.def: ῥῠ́σις, εως, (ῥέω) I. a flowing, flow, Plat. II. the course of a river, stream, Polyb.

ρυσκομαι.def: ῥύσκομαι, (= ῥύομαι· ῥύσκευ, epic 2nd sg. imperf., Il.)

ρυσοσ.def: ῥῡσός, ή, όν (⁎ῥύω, ἐρύω) drawn up, shrivelled, wrinkled, Il., Eur., etc.; ῥ. ἐπισκύνιον, of a frown, Anth.

ρυσοτησ.def: ῥῡσότης, ητος, ἡ, (from ῥῡσός) wrinkledness, wrinkles, Plut.

ρυσταζω.def: ῥυστάζω, (Frequentat. of ⁎ῥύω) (= ἐρύω) to drag about, πολλὰ ῥυστάζεσκεν (3rd sg. ionic imperf.) περὶ σῆμα he dragged it many times round the grave of Patroclus, Il.; δμωὰς ῥυστάζειν κατὰ δώματα, Od.

ρυστακτυσ.def: ῥυστακτύς, ύος, ἡ, (from ῥυστάζω) a dragging about, maltreatment, Od.

ρυταγωγευσ.gloss: the rope of a horse's halter
ρυταγωγευσ.def: ῥῡτ-ᾰγωγεύς, έως, ὁ, the rope of a horse's halter, Xen.

ρυτηρ.def: ῥῡτηφαιλινγ ον λεμβυφ [] (⁎ῥύω, ἐρύω) I. one who draws or stretches, ῥ. βιοῦ, ὀϊστῶν drawer of the bow, of arrows, Od. 2. like ἱμάς, the strap by which a horse draws, a trace, Il.:—also a rein, id.; ἀπὸ ῥυτῆρος with loose rein, Lat. immissis habenis, at full galop:—used as a strap to flog with, Dem., Aeschin. II. （ῥύομαι) a saver, guard, defender, Od.

ρυτιδοφλοιοσ.def: ῥῠτῐδό-φλοιος, ον, with shrivelled rind, σῦκον Anth.

ρυτιδοω.def: ῥῠτῐδόω, (ῥυτίς) to make wrinkled:—Pass. to be so, perf. part. ἐρρυτιδωμένος Luc.

ρυτισ.def: ῥῠτίς, ίδος, ἡ, (ῥύω, ἐρύω) a fold or pucker in the face, a wrinkle, Lat. ruga, Ar., Plat.

ρυτον.def: ῥῠτόν, οῦ, (⁎ῥύω, ἐρύω) (= ῥυτήρ) I. a rein, Hes. II. （ῥέω) a drinking-cup, running to a point with a small hole, through which the wine ran, Dem.

ρυτοσ.def: ῥῡτός, ή, όν (⁎ῥύω, ἐρύω) dragged along, ῥυτοὶ λάες stones dragged along, i. e. too large to carry, Od.
ῥῠτός, ή, όν (ῥέω) flowing, running, fluid, liquid, Trag.

ρυτωρ.def: ῥῡ́τωρ, ορος, ὁ, (ῥύομαι) a saviour, deliverer, Aesch., Anth.; τινός from a thing, id.

ρυω.def: Ῥύω, whence ἐρύω, to draw (v. ῥύομαι.)

ρω.def: ῥῶ I. Ρ, ρ, ῥῶ, τό, indecl., seventeenth letter of Gr. Alphabet, as numeral ρʹ = 100, but ͵ρ = 100,000. Dialectic and other changes: 1. aeolic, at the end of words ς passed into ρ, as οὗτορ, ἵππορ for οὗτος, ἵππος; cf. Lat. arbor arbos, honor honos. 2. in attic, ρρ replaced the ionic and old attic ρς, as ἄρρην, θάρρος for ἄρσην, θάρσος. 3. in some words ρ is transposed, as κάρτος epic for κράτος, ἀταρπός for ἀτραπός, κραδίη for καρδία:—mostly in Poets. II. ρ at the beginning of a word was pronounced so as to make a short vowel at the end of the word before long by position, as, ψυχρὴ ὑπὸ ῥιπῆς Il. 2. by reason of this pronunc., ρ was doubled after a prep. or α privat., and after the augment, as ἀπορρίπτω, ἄρρωστος, ἔρριψα. 3. if ρ begins a word, it takes the rough breathing, except in aeolic

ρωγαλεοσ.def: ῥωγᾰλέος, η, ον, (ῥώξ) broken, cleft, rent, torn, Hom.

ρωγασ.def: ῥωγάς, άδος, (ῥώξ) (= ῥωγᾰλέος) ragged, Babr.; ῥ. πέτρα a cloven rock, Theocr.

ρωθων.def: ῥώθων, ωνος, ὁ, the nose: in pl. the nostrils, Strab.

ρωμαικοσ.def: Ῥωμαϊκός, ή, όν Roman, a Roman, Polyb., etc.; adv. -κῶς, in Latin, Anth.

ρωμαλεοσ.def: ῥωμᾰλέος, η, ον, (ῥώμη) 1. strong of body, Plat. 2. of things, mighty, strong, Hdt.

ρωμη.def: ῥώμη, ἡ, (ῥώομαι) I. bodily strength, strength, might, Hdt., Trag., etc.; οὐ μιᾷ ῥώμῃ not single-handed, Soph. II. a force, i. e. army, Xen.

ρωννυμι.gloss: to strengthen, make strong and mighty
ρωννυμι.def: ῥώννυμι (ῥώομαι) I. to strengthen, make strong and mighty, Plut. II. mostly in perf. pass. (with pres. sense) ἔρρωμαι, and plup. ἐρρώμην (as imperf.):— to put forth strength, have strength or might, Eur., Thuc.:—c. inf. to have strength to do, be eager to do, Thuc. 2. often in imperat., ἔρρωσο, farewell, Lat. vale, Xen.; also, φράζειν τινὶ ἐρρῶσθαι, Lat. valere jubere, Plat. 3. part. ἐρρωμένος, ῥωμαλέος, v. sub voce.

ρωξ.def: ῥώξ, ῥωγός, (ῥήγνυμι) a cleft: in Od., ῥῶγες μεγάροιο are narrow passages leading to the hall.

ρωομαι.def: ῥώομαι, to move with speed or violence, to dart, rush, rush on, Hom.; ῥ. περὶ πυρήν Od.; ἀμφ’ Ἀχελώιον ἐρρώσαντο danced about Achelous, Il.; χορὸν ἐρρώσαντο plied the lusty dance, Hhymn.; ὑπὸ ῥώοντο ἄνακτι lustily they moved under the king's weight, Il.; so, γούνατα ἐρρώσαντο Od.; also of the hair, ἐρρώοντο μετὰ πνοιῇς ἀνέμοιο it waved streaming in the wind, Il.

ρωπηιον.def: ῥωπήιον, ου, τό, (ῥώψ) (only in pl. ῥωπήια) brushes, brushwood, Il.

ρωπικοσ.def: ῥωπικός, ή, όν (ῥῶπος) of or for petty wares, trumpery, worthless, Plut.; ῥωπικὰ γράψασθαι to paint poorly, coarsely, Anth.

ρωποσ.def: ῥῶπος, ὁ, petty wares, Aesch., Dem.

ρωχμοσ.def: ῥωχμός, οῦ, ὁ, (ῥώξ) a cleft, ῥωχμὸς γαίης a gutter scooped out by heavy rains, Il.

ρωψ.def: ῥώψ, ῥωπός, a shrub, bush: only pl. bushes, underwood, brushwood, Od. Od.
